audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Locke level 6 and first item and called 2+ items Skill, while whys[4], whys[5] and whys[6] say even, even, and Dr. Mundo. The packet chart agrees with the whys.
audit.why: Nothing about Purgatory beats a champion who heals a percentage of missing health on demand; the lane is genuinely flat until his HP items land, and then it is his. The mirror settled on Skill through First item with Dr. Mundo at 2+ items.
audit.corrected: Rows 4 and 5 flipped to Skill, row 6 to Dr. Mundo, in BOTH layers, with ratings 5/5/3 and the two Locke-arguing why lines rewritten. EVEN 5.5/10 overall kept — 45.92% over 858 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Trade when his cleaver is on cooldown' is the core instruction and Infected Bonesaw's cooldown was never given.
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw is 4 seconds flat and costs no mana — there is effectively no cooldown window to wait for, so the advice as written is unusable. The real trackable cooldowns are Heart Zapper at 17s and Maximum Dosage at a flat 120s.
audit.corrected: The 4s cleaver stated in early so the reader stops waiting for a window that does not come; 17s Heart Zapper given as the actual step-up cue; 120s on his R.

audit.whatIsWrong: Infected Bonesaw was called percent-MAX-health; Maximum Dosage was called an overheal of max health; Locke's Q was called Ritual Nails and his passive Silver Stake.
audit.why: Riot's Q text is damage based on the target's CURRENT health — it hits hardest when you are full and tapers as you drop, the opposite of how the page reads. Maximum Dosage instantly heals a percent of MISSING health then regenerates over time, so it is strongest exactly when he is low, which is what actually beats an execute. Locke's Q is Soul Nails and his passive is unnamed in the file.
audit.corrected: Current-health cleaver and missing-health heal stated; Soul Nails used; the passive described by its missing-health on-hit effect.

audit.whatIsWrong: His passive resists the FIRST immobilising effect that hits him, dropping a cannister he can walk over to heal and shorten the cooldown — the page only says he 'shrugs off your CC'.
audit.why: It means the first hard CC your team lands is wasted, and letting him collect the cannister refunds him health on top. Denying or contesting the cannister is a real play.
audit.corrected: Stated in late with the cannister pickup named.

edits.before: Purgatory online: top lane's long brawls now end at YOUR floor. Anyone who all-ins you under a third is volunteering for the totem.
edits.after: Purgatory sets a floor, but Maximum Dosage heals a percent of MISSING health on cast — it is strongest exactly where your execute lives. Even.

edits.before: Lich Bane spike — the blink-consume chunk finally out-numbers their sustain. Cash kill windows before their second item re-rigs the math.
edits.after: Lich Bane bites, but his regen answers it. Still even: bring Grievous Wounds and cash a window while his health bar is one item thin.

edits.before: Even skill window — your Q Ritual Nails poke and P Silver Stake missing-HP procs actually punish Mundo's passive-regen tankiness, but respect his Q Infected Bonesaw cleaver which chunks a percent of your HP and slows.
edits.after: Even skill window — your Q Soul Nails poke and missing-HP on-hits genuinely punish Mundo's regen, but respect Q Infected Bonesaw: it is up every 4s, free to cast, and hits off your CURRENT health, so it stings most at full.

edits.before: Still even at 6 — your R Purgatory can threaten a low Mundo, but his R Maximum Dosage heals a huge chunk of max HP on cast, letting him climb back above your execute threshold mid-fight.
edits.after: Still even at 6 — your R Purgatory threatens a low Mundo, but Maximum Dosage instantly heals a percent of his MISSING health, so the lower you push him the more it gives back. Bait the 120s first.

edits.before: Late game tips to Mundo — his stacked HP and R Maximum Dosage overheal outrun your R threshold, and his passive shrugs off your CC while E scales its damage off his own huge health bar.
edits.after: Late game tips to Mundo — stacked HP plus a missing-health R outruns your threshold, his passive eats the first immobilise outright, and E Blunt Force Trauma scales off his own missing health.

edits.before: Levels 1-5 are an even, skill-based lane. Your Q Ritual Nails and P Silver Stake missing-HP on-hit are two of the few tools that actually pressure a passive-regen tank, so trade whenever his Q Infected Bonesaw cleaver is on cooldown and deny him free stacking. Don't stand in the cleaver's path — it deals percent-max-HP and slows you into his walk-up.
edits.after: Levels 1-5 are an even, skill-based lane. Your Q Soul Nails and missing-HP on-hits are two of the few tools that pressure a regen tank, so bite after he spends Heart Zapper, 17s at rank 1, rather than waiting on his cleaver — that is 4s and free. Don't stand in its path: it hits off your current health and slows you into his walk-up.

edits.before: Level 6 stays even. Your R Purgatory threatens a low Mundo, but the instant he casts R Maximum Dosage he overheals a large chunk of max HP and climbs back above your execute threshold, so time your ult for after his R or bait it out. Your W Soul Ignition self-damage is risky here because his sustained cleaver poke can leave you unable to afford the grey-health cost.
edits.after: Level 6 stays even. Your R Purgatory threatens a low Mundo, but Maximum Dosage instantly restores a percent of his MISSING health — the deeper you burn him, the more it returns — so spend your 120s only after his. Your W Soul Ignition self-damage is risky here because his 4s cleaver poke leaves you unable to afford the grey-health cost.

edits.before: Late game belongs to Dr. Mundo. Stacked HP items plus R Maximum Dosage overheal push his effective health far past your R's growing threshold, his passive tosses your CC on the ground, and E Blunt Force Trauma scales harder as his own health balloons. Look to roam and take side lanes rather than solo-killing an untouchable Mundo.
edits.after: Late game belongs to Dr. Mundo. HP items plus a missing-health R push him far past your threshold, his passive resists the first immobilise and drops a cannister that heals him again if he walks over it, and E Blunt Force Trauma hits harder the lower he gets. Roam and take side lanes rather than forcing a solo kill.

edits.before: Level 6 is even — your R threat is answered by his R Maximum Dosage overheal.
edits.after: Level 6 is even — his R heals a percent of missing health on cast.

edits.after: Land Q Infected Bonesaw for current-health poke and a slow

edits.after: Cast R Maximum Dosage to heal missing HP past your threshold

edits.before: Bait his Q Infected Bonesaw cleaver then E Ashen Pursuit in
edits.after: Bait his W Heart Zapper, then E Ashen Pursuit in on him

notes: The biggest single error here was directional: the page told the reader to trade 'when the cleaver is on cooldown' (it is 4s and free) and described Maximum Dosage as a max-health overheal when it scales off MISSING health — which reverses the advice about pushing him low. Heart Zapper also stores damage he takes and heals off it on the burst, so Grievous Wounds applied before that burst is the real counter-play; report[8] already calls for anti-heal. E Blunt Force Trauma scales off Dr. Mundo's own missing health, not his max health, and the old spikes[3] had that backwards too.
